overall_explanation: Reviewed the new codex-linux-pidfd-spawn crate (ffi.rs, spawn.rs, spawn_tests.rs), workspace/lock/Bazel wiring, and the QA evidence. The unsafe boundary is coherent: version-pinned dlvsym lookup of pidfd_spawn@GLIBC_2.39 (the version that introduced it), non-p variant so ENOEXEC has no shell/PATH fallback, MaybeUninit-backed spawn attrs/actions with RAII destroy on every early-return path, SIG_IGN/SA_NOCLDWAIT SIGCHLD guard, chdir '/', null stdio, explicit close of 3..image_fd plus closefrom(image_fd+1) with the CLOEXEC-verified image retained only until exec, empty env, and immediate OwnedFd adoption of the returned pidfd. spawn.rs validates fd range (3..=256), memfd seals, CLOEXEC and PROC_SUPER_MAGIC before building the /proc/self/fd path; the image OwnedFd is dropped after spawn so no descriptor leaks (confirmed by fd-count tests). Non-root gating happens before launch. OwnedChild retains the pidfd on error, terminate() treats ESRCH as success, and Drop's kill/NOHANG-wait retry loop breaks on exit or ECHILD; the unbounded-block behavior is explicitly documented as an embedding precondition rather than a hidden defect. rustix 1.1.4 APIs (waitid PidFd returning Option<WaitIdStatus>, Copy WaitIdStatus, pidfd_send_signal<AsFd>) match the local registry source. Crate is fully cfg-gated to linux-gnu + synthetic-fixture, so default builds and non-Linux targets are unaffected; Cargo.lock entry and Bazel BUILD follow existing crate patterns (no cross-crate list needs updating). Tests are per-process under nextest, restore rlimits before asserting, and fail rather than skip on missing fixtures. No exploitable security exposure, crash, leak, or landability blocker found within the frozen scope.
